analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 19, 2026)
key_insights: Asia lagged a recovery in US and EU futures, dragged by AI-supply-chain-exposed names and weak China tech earnings. TWSE is down over 10% on the week on AI capex fears, and stock market stabilization measures were announced, including an expanded short selling ban.

Technicals favor a near-term AI bounce. Positioning, sentiment and drawdowns create an asymmetric setup, with the market pricing negative Semis EPS growth after 2027 and the 'Capex Peak' scenario. Revisions, with focus on 2028 forecasts, are the key risk.

HK Tech Conference feedback was bearish: investors are trading the end of the AI cycle well before companies see it. Three camps of negativity: price momentum (stocks not responding to good news), fundamental (AI stocks can't rise without 2028 capex visibility), and cyber (a large, growing, idiosyncratic 'known unknown').

SEC data show a lower share of retail investors in US equity trading in Q3, suggesting less retail involvement in the July Tech unwind and bounce. If this holds in Q4, the latest AI unwind and rotation would be institutionally driven.

Expectations are low for the first Trump/Xi/Putin trilateral at APEC. AI developments are watched given fresh US export restrictions, and rare earths are China's edge. The Iran war shows no sign of abating.
Oil is held lower by an oversupply narrative. API reported a substantial US crude and gas inventory build.

Gold broke below key technical levels, with next support at $3605. Hawkish Fed speak has not helped, but Positioning Intelligence flags that the short-led capitulation in gold could drive near-term upside.

Copper selloff is tied to the peak AI capex narrative, with China dynamics also at play: the Yangshan Premium over the LME benchmark reached a multi-decade high, making it more economic to import copper from the US, where inventory has built on tariff expectations.

Luxury conference feedback: company tone was subdued and a step down from last year, pointing to a difficult global environment and weak footfall, especially in China. Companies expect muted pricing into next year, so a 2027 reacceleration depends on each brand's execution. Jewellery and high-end ready-to-wear were bright spots.

UK CPI rose to 3.6% y/y in October but undershot BoE forecasts across food, core and services. Lower market energy prices suggest continued undershoot next year. Data this week were dovish and lowered the odds of a December BoE hike.

Euro area inflation was 4.0% y/y headline in the final release, with core revised up marginally to 2.6%. HICP gas and electricity prices were significantly higher in October. JPM still expects core to rise to 2.8% y/y at the start of 2027.

JPM Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities. Broadening and international (ex-US) have led over the past month on ex-AI rotation and US midterm implications. EU outperformance is supported by about 13% median y/y Q3 EPS growth, the same as the US, and by relative positioning vs the US reaching extreme lows.

The tactical Tech bounce case, led by US/APAC Semis and AI themes, rests on solid fundamentals (AI unit economics, scaling laws, token growth), valuations implying imminent EPS cuts, and no classic cycle-peak signals such as inventory builds or shorter lead times. The bounce is technical and short-term, with a less V-shaped recovery than H1 because buyside capex expectations show signs of peaking.

Positioning Intelligence: HF net flows in US Semis were below -3z for a second week, and HF selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record. Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025, and the global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x.

Semis exposure remains around the 80th percentile since 2018, and HF positioning z-score is below the relative returns z-score, so history suggests a rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.

HF gross flows stabilized after near -2z de-grossing Monday, with Thursday the most positive global re-gross day in about a month. HF performance rose about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat month to date globally, with Europe up 1.7% MTD and Asia down 2%.

US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 20th percentile since 2015. Relative EU vs US positioning is back to neutral after European flows rose 1.5z relative to US flows over 1-3 months. Japan HF flows were -1.4z WoW and -2.3z MoM, with combined Japan positioning at the 24th percentile since 2015.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term tactical bounce favored on depressed positioning and sentiment, but the bounce is seen as technical and short-term given capex peak concerns.
Company tone was subdued, China is deteriorating again and pricing is expected to stay muted into next year.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning, sentiment and drawdowns are extreme: HF net exposure down 67% from peak, six straight weeks of HF selling, very bearish retail sentiment and QQQ short interest. Valuations imply imminent EPS cuts and no classic cycle-peak signals appear.
tension_points.bear_case: Buyside capex expectations show signs of peaking, the rotation out of AI may extend on funding pressure, AI ARR trends are in question, and Semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A shift in 2028 capex and EPS revisions, or HF positioning z-score staying below the relative returns z-score without HFs turning more bullish.
